sentence: This project develops methods to make gene-edited hematopoietic stem cells for clinical trials in patients with blood cancers.
This project studies how a nuclear protein controls the metabolism and functions of T lymphocytes that fight cancer.
This project uses gene editing to find what changes blood cell function with age and how blood cell mutations affect muscle and other organs.
This project studies how gene mutations in a rare blood disease that causes anemia harm the function of hematopoietic stem cells.
This project studies what human genes do in single cells during early development, using a technology that manipulates genes.
This project tries to find which cell pathways and proteins are faulty in mouse retinas with mutations linked to retinal degenerative diseases.
This project builds a core that gives bioinformatics and modeling help to study immune responses to pathogens and disease states.
This project studies how progestins work and why they fail in some women with endometrial cancer.
This project tries to find out why Plasmodium infections continue in villages despite malaria control efforts.
This project studies how inflammatory signaling and transcription factors disrupt the development of erythrocytes, using human cells.
This project builds a technology that maps proteins in cells and tissues at single-molecule resolution using multiplexed imaging.
This project runs CRISPR screens that knock out single genes in cultured cells to find genes that control aging.
This project studies how two antibodies bind gonococcal lipooligosaccharide and uses this to design antibodies against multidrug-resistant gonorrhea.
This project builds machine learning tools that predict what proteins and chemicals do.
This project studies how cannabis use and sleep affect each other over time, along with hypothalamic pituitary adrenal axis activity.
This project develops imaging probes that use positron emission tomography to track activated T cells in cancer immunotherapy.
This project makes insulin-producing cells for diabetes treatment and tests that they are safe and not rejected by the immune system.
This project develops a vaccine made from cancer stem cells to fight glioblastoma by using the immune system.
This project links brain organoids to a computer model built from large datasets to find drug treatments for neurological diseases.
This project studies how a form of programmed cell death called necroptosis drives inflammation and liver injury in alcohol-associated liver disease.
